text:
Aisha Khan: Heads up — we've got a growing wave of DNS failures hitting GPU provisioner in apac-edge and us-west-edge. Pods can fetch images but model-server healthchecks fail with NXDOMAIN for internal model registry host. Starts ~04:12 UTC. :eyes:
Tom Lee: saw this too, looks like NXDOMAINs are sticky for ~90s then clear. Any change in TTLs or negative caching?
Devin Patel: I pulled a few dig traces from node-local-dns and a worker that hit NAT:
```
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;registry.internal.redwood.io. IN A
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
internal.redwood.io. 300 IN SOA ns1.internal.redwood.io. hostmaster 2026031801 3600 600 604800 60
;; SERVER: 10.0.0.10#53(10.0.0.10)
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, rcode: NXDOMAIN, id: 41234
```
Ben Ortiz: interesting — SOA negative TTL is 60s there, but the node-local-dns cache is returning NXDOMAIN for 5x that. Any chance we're seeing transaction ID / port collision because of SNAT?
Aisha Khan: how would SNAT cause prolonged NXDOMAIN?
Ben Ortiz: hypothesis: our egress NAT buckets are reusing source ports quickly (ephemeral exhaustion), combined with UDP retries routing to a different authoritative server that responds NXDOMAIN for certain split-horizon names. Node-local-dns or systemd-resolved may cache based on (query->response) and miss the mismatch. Also some nodes use systemd-resolved stub which keeps a longer negative cache.
dns-prober-bot: probe summary: 48/120 failures last 10m from apac-edge egress pool-7, 0 TCP fallback seen. Average source port reuse density 0.34 (high).
Tom Lee: confirmed we see very few TCP fallbacks. iptables SNAT shows many connections hitting the same ephemeral ports quickly. Also conntrack table pressure on NAT gateway.
Devin Patel: dug deeper, here's the node-local-dns log excerpt (condensed):
```
2026-03-18T04:12:23Z node-dns: query id=41234 name=registry.internal.redwood.io src=10.244.0.12
2026-03-18T04:12:23Z upstream: sent id=41234 to 100.64.1.5:53 via SNAT src-port=55012
2026-03-18T04:12:23Z upstream: recv id=41234 rcode=NXDOMAIN from 100.64.1.6:53
2026-03-18T04:12:23Z cache: write NXDOMAIN ttl=60 key=registry.internal.redwood.io
2026-03-18T04:12:24Z upstream: recv id=41234 rcode=NOERROR from 100.64.1.7:53
2026-03-18T04:12:24Z cache: ??? ignored NOERROR for same id
```
Aisha Khan: whoa — downstream got two different authoritative responses for the same ID, different upstream IPs. That explains the cache inconsistency.
Tom Lee: root cause plausibly: SNAT port reuse + non-deterministic authoritative server responses -> stale NXDOMAIN persisted in the caching tier. We should force TCP fallback for these queries or prefer UDP source port randomization.
Ben Ortiz: quick mitigation options:
- increase ephemeral port range on NAT gateways (reduces reuse)
- enable TCP transport for resolver pool (less likely with UDP port reuse)
- make node-local-dns respect per upstream IP caches (avoid conflating responses by id alone)
- short-term: set an iptables rule to MASQUERADE with a larger port range for apac-edge pool-7
Devin Patel: also we can add a patch to node-local-dns to key cache by (qname,qtype,upstream-ip) rather than ID-only. Longer term we should add TCP fallback for critical internal names (model registry, image registry).
Aisha Khan: can we prioritize quick infra changes today? Which is lowest-risk?
Tom Lee: increasing ephemeral port range + bumping conntrack thresholds is safest and revertible. I can roll a change to nat-gateway pool-7 now.
Ben Ortiz: I'll open a node-local-dns PR to make caching less brittle (won't land today). Also enabling TCP fallback by default for internal zones would be good; needs testing (possible perf impact).
dns-prober-bot: patch candidate: nat-gw-7-ephemeral-range expanded 32768-61000 -> applied to staging.
Aisha Khan: thanks. After the nat change we should watch dns-prober and the model-server healthchecks. Assigning follow-up: @Tom Lee to monitor, @Ben Ortiz to track PR, @Devin Patel to run a controlled canary across 10 nodes. :thumbsup:
Tom Lee: rolling now to pool-7, will report in 5m.
Devin Patel: quick note — for debugging, if you hit this: run `tcpdump -n -i any udp port 53 or tcp port 53` on the node and verify upstream IPs and src ports. Also `ss -tun sport = :53` won't show UDP ephemeral; use conntrack.
Aisha Khan: great, keep updates here. If we see recurrence we'll open incident and revert traffic to a different egress pool.
Tom Lee: update: after ephemeral range bump failures dropped from 40% -> 3% in 7m. Healthchecks recovered. Leaving monitoring on. :white_check_mark:
Ben Ortiz: filed PR 342 for node-local-dns caching keying and an RFC for enabling TCP fallback on critical zones.
Aisha Khan: nice work team, we'll run the PR through the usual cycle. Closing thread unless anything else pops up. :wave:
